AGENDA

  CITY COUNCIL/PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
  Monday, December 2, 2019
  Council Chambers
  2000 Main Street
  Huntington Beach, CA 92648

  No Study Session / No Closed Session
  Regular Meeting - 6:00 PM

  MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL
  ERIK PETERSON, Mayor

  ALISA BACKSTROM, City Treasurer

MEETING ASSISTANCE NOTICE: In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, services are available to members
of our community who require special assistance to participate in public meetings. If you require special assistance,
48-hour prior notification will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements for an assisted listening device (ALD) for the
hearing impaired, American Sign Language interpreters, a reader during the meeting and/or large print agendas. Please
contact the City Clerk’s Office at (714) 536-5227 for more information, or request assistance from the staff or
Sergeant-at-Arms at the meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS: To address the legislative body on items of interest not scheduled for public hearing, Request to
Speak forms will be made available at the meeting and are collected by the staff or Sergeant at Arms. Some legislative
bodies may provide different Request to Speak forms for public hearing items.

AUDIO/VIDEO ACCESS TO BROADCASTED MEETINGS: City Council and Planning Commission meetings are televised live
on HBTV-3 Channel 3, and can be viewed via live or archived website at https://huntingtonbeach.legistar.com.

{\*\generator Riched20 5.40.11.2210;}\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Tim Whitacre, was called to speak, and on behalf of Michelle Steele, Chairman of the Board of Supervisors, 2nd District, thanked Mayor Peterson for his year of leading with honor, distinction, and transparency, and presented a Certificate of Recognition.  Mr. Whitacre also congratulated Incoming Mayor Semeta on behalf of Supervisor Steele.\par
\par
Don MacAllister was called to speak and stated his support for the City's Sister City relationships, and enthusiasm for Consent Calendar Item No. 3 regarding extending a Sister City Relationship invitation to the City of Biarritz, France.\par
\par
Frank Nakabayashi was called to speak and stated his support for the City's Sister City relationships, and enthusiasm for Consent Calendar Item No. 3 regarding extending a Sister City Relationship invitation to the City of Biarritz, France.\par
\par
Calvin ("Mr. Huntington Beach") and Pam Free were called to speak and presented Mayor Peterson with his own loudspeaker and read a limerick in his honor.\par
\par
Jericho Poppler was called to speak and presented Mayor Peterson with some fresh, homemade Scottish shortbread, and thanked the City Council for their service on behalf of the City's surfers.\par
\par
Diana Dehm was called to speak and thanked the City Council for their support in putting out to bid the lease for the Surf City International Surf Museum, and congratulated Outgoing Mayor Peterson and Incoming Mayor Semeta.\par
\par
Bob Pace was called to speak and thanked the City Council for putting out to bid the lease for the Surf City International Surf Museum.\par
\par
Cari Swan was called to speak and thanked Mayor Peterson for always honoring his promises to the citizens of Huntington Beach, and congratulated Incoming Mayor Semeta and Incoming Mayor Pro Tem Hardy.  Ms. Swan also shared her concerns about the Magnolia Tank Farm and Ascon remediation projects.\par
\par
Gary Sahagan was called to speak and thanked the City Council for putting out to bid the lease for the Surf City International Surf Museum.\par
\par
Grant Sevdayan, Music Director, Huntington Beach Symphony Orchestra, was called to speak and shared a video with clips of various performances.\par
\par
Judith Lopez, Huntington Beach Symphony Orchestra Member, was called to speak and for proper acoustical requirements, asked for a special exemption to allow the Orchestra to perform in the City Hall Amphitheatre for July 4th festivities.  Mayor Peterson asked Ms. Lopez to complete a blue card for staff follow-up.\par
\par
Rob Pool was called to speak and congratulated Mayor Peterson for a spectacular year of service, encouraged Mayor Pro Tem Semeta to remain true to her values, and acknowledged Incoming Mayor Pro Tem Hardy for always looking for what is best for the City.  Mr. Pool further shared his thoughts regarding the Magnolia Tank Farm and Ascon remediation projects.\par
\par
Adam Orozco was called to speak and thanked Mayor Peterson and the Council members for their service.\par
\par
Joyce Bizzaro, a local surfer and member of the Huntington Beach International Surf Museum, was called to speak and thanked the City Council for putting out to bid the lease for the Surf Museum.\par
\par
Kim Weddon, representing the Huntington Harbour Philharmonic Islanders, was called to speak and thanked Mayor Peterson for his service and congratulated Incoming Mayor Semeta, and explained the Philharmonic's purpose is music education in the local schools.  The Annual Holiday Cruise of Lights is their major fundraiser, and Ms. Weddon expressed appreciation for Incoming Mayor Semeta's support and participation.\par
\par
Patricia McKenna, President,  Huntington Harbour Art Association, was called to speak and thanked Council members for their service, and congratulated Incoming Mayor Semeta, a member of the Harbour Art Association.\par
\par
Dee Wood, representing the Huntington Harbour Book Club, was called to speak and thanked Mayor Peterson for his service and congratulated Incoming Mayor Semeta\par
\par
Matthew Harper, Huntington Beach homeowner and Former Mayor, was called to speak and congratulated Mayor Peterson for his year of service, and expressed his best wishes for Incoming Mayor Semeta.\par
\par
Dave Sullivan, Huntington Beach Former Mayor and Police Officer, was called to speak and thanked Mayor Peterson for his "get'r done" Marine service as Mayor this past year, and congratulated Incoming Mayor Semeta.\par
\par
Tim Geddes, a 35+ year resident of south east Huntington Beach, was called to speak and congratulated both Mayor Peterson and Incoming Mayor Semeta.  Mr. Geddes also shared his concerns related to the Pso Desalination Plant, Magnolia Tank Farm, Ascon remediation projects.\par
\par
Amber was called to speak\par
